t.1.198.1: The wise Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, and the blessed seer Droṇa have spoken words of the highest benefit, and you too speak the truth to me.
t.1.198.2: Just as those heroic sons of Kuntī, great chariot-warriors, are Pāṇḍu's, so too, by dharma and in every respect, they are my sons; there is no doubt.
t.1.198.3: Just as this kingdom is ordained for my sons, so too is this kingdom for the sons of Pāṇḍu; of that there is no doubt.
t.1.198.4: Go, Kṣattar, and bring them here, well honored, together with their mother, and together with that godlike Kṛṣṇā, O Bhārata.
t.1.198.5: By good fortune those Pārthas are alive, by good fortune Pṛthā lives, and by good fortune the great chariot-warriors have won the daughter of Drupada.
t.1.198.6: By good fortune we all prosper; by good fortune Purocana has been quieted; by good fortune my supreme sorrow has been taken away, O greatly splendid one.
t.1.198.7: Then, at the command of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Vidura went to Yajñasena and to the Pāṇḍavas, O Bhārata.
t.1.198.9: He too then received Vidura in accordance with dharma, and the two, as was fitting, engaged in an exchange of inquiries about each other's welfare.
t.1.198.8: Having gone there, O king, he, the knower of dharma, learned in all the śāstras, approached Drupada, who was joined with the Pāṇḍavas, in due and proper form.
t.1.198.10: There, O Bhārata, he saw the Pāṇḍavas and Vāsudeva; embracing them with affection, he then asked after their well-being.
t.1.198.11: And he of boundless intelligence was then honored by them in turn, in due order; and at the word of Dhṛtarāṣṭra he spoke affectionately, again and again.
t.1.198.12: Then, O king, he asked after the well-being of those sons of Pāṇḍu, and he also bestowed upon them jewels of many kinds and riches.
t.1.198.13: For the Pāṇḍavas, for Kuntī and for Draupadī, O lord of the people, and for the sons of Drupada, just as they had been given by the Kauravas.
t.1.198.14: And he of boundless wisdom, endowed with modesty, spoke courteously to Drupada in the presence of the sons of Pāṇḍu and of Keśava.
t.1.198.16: Delighted again and again, O king, he asked after your welfare, and he is also firmly pleased with your alliance, O lord of men.
t.1.198.15: O king, listen to my words, together with your ministers and your sons: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, with his sons, his ministers and his kinsmen, greets you.
t.1.198.17: Likewise Bhīṣma, the son of Śaṃtanu, the greatly wise one, together with all the Kauravas, asks after your welfare in every respect.
t.1.198.18: Droṇa, the descendant of Bharadvāja, the great archer and your dear friend, embracing you, asks after your welfare.
t.1.198.19: And Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O Pāñcālya, having entered into a marriage alliance with you, considers himself to have attained his aim, and so too do all the Kauravas.
t.1.198.20: The attainment of the kingdom is not deemed so pleasing to them as the gaining of this alliance with you, O Yajñasena.
t.1.198.21: Knowing this, may you send forth the Pāṇḍavas, for the Kurus are exceedingly eager to see the heirs of Pāṇḍu.
t.1.198.22: These bulls among men, too, having lived away from home for a long time, will be eager to see the city, and so will Pṛthā.
t.1.198.24: Let your honor, without delay, give leave for the departure of the sons of Pāṇḍu together with their wife; this is the purpose of my coming.
t.1.198.23: All the noble women of the Kurus, eager to see Kṛṣṇā Pāñcālī too, are waiting for her, and so too are our city and our realm.
t.1.198.25: When the great-souled Pāṇḍavas have been dismissed by you, O king, I shall then send Dhṛtarāṣṭra's swift messengers; the sons of Kuntī will come, and Kuntī too, together with Kṛṣṇā.
